parts:
glmmTMB questions (which this one appears to be) are probably better
suited for r-sig-mix...@r-project.org *or* the glmmTMB issues list
<https://github.com/glmmtmb/glmmTMB/issues>.

I don't know exactly what your problem is, but here are three minimal
examples that show that glmmTMB does not handle *either* scale() or
data-dependent bases (poly(), splines::ns(), etc.) correctly:

library(glmmTMB)
data("sleepstudy",package="lme4")

g1 <- glmmTMB(Reaction~poly(Days,3), sleepstudy)
predict(g1, newdata=data.frame(Days=0))

library(splines)
g2 <- glmmTMB(Reaction~ns(Days,5), sleepstudy)
predict(g2, newdata=data.frame(Days=0))

g3 <- glmmTMB(Reaction~scale(Days), sleepstudy)
predict(g3, newdata=data.frame(Days=0))

I'm going to go ahead and post this to the issues list myself since at
first glance it appears to be a serious bug. (Hopefully I'm being hasty
and it's not as bad as it seems ...)

On 2018-10-17 5:54 p.m., Michael Whitby wrote:
> Hello,
>
> I have a model specified with a polynomial and scale terms.
> Specifically, the model formula is:
>
> nLABO ~ (1 | GRID) + (1 | NIGHT) + poly(DAYofYR, 5) + scale(HEIGHT) +
> night_hrs + scale(nTMP) + nUwind + nVwind + scale(nPRES) +
> scale(nPresChange) + scale(nRH) + scale(nCloud) + scale(nTotRain) +
> scale(nHRSRAIN) + scale(nMoon)
>
> predict works perfectly fine when I use a held back portion of my
> dataset. However if I create new data in order to evaluate individual
> term effects, predict is returning 'NaN' for all values.
>
> newdata <-expand.grid( GRID = factor("new",levels=levels(df_Train$GRID)),
> NIGHT = factor("2015-07-29",levels=levels(df_Train$NIGHT)),
> DAYofYR = as.integer(seq(120, 300, by = 1)),
> HEIGHT = as.integer(65),
> night_hrs = mean(df_Train$night_hrs),
> nTMP= mean(df_Train$nTMP),
> nUwind = mean(df_Train$nUwind),
> nVwind = mean(df_Train$nVwind),
> nPRES = mean(df_Train$nPRES),
> nPresChange = mean(df_Train$nPresChange),
> nRH = mean(df_Train$nRH),
> nCloud = mean(df_Train$nCloud),
> nTotRain = 0,
> nHRSRAIN = 0,
> nMoon = 0 )
>
>
> test <- predict(dist.best, newdata, type="link", allow.new.levels = T)
>
> I'll work to simulate a dataset for a reproducible example, but am
> hoping somebody knows why this is happening before I figure that out.
